destination.name: Forster
destination.tagline: A summer holiday town on Wallis Lake with a chain of surf and family beaches to its south.
destination.description: Forster and its twin town Tuncurry sit either side of an inlet joined by a long causeway, and Wikivoyage calls the area a place of summer pilgrimage for Sydney families. Booti Booti National Park, a peninsula between the ocean and Wallis Lake, holds Cape Hawke Lookout and an 8 km loop walk. South of town are Elizabeth, Boomerang and Blueys beaches, while Diamond Beach runs six kilometres towards Taree.
whyVisit: Climb the steps to Cape Hawke Lookout
Walk the length of Diamond Beach

goodToKnow.title: Whales pass May to November
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage gives May to November for whale watching; Bennetts Head Lookout in town is wheelchair accessible.

goodToKnow.title: Pick the beach for the day
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage rates Elizabeth Beach as a shallow family beach, Boomerang as the best for surfing, Blueys as long and shallow, and Diamond as long and quiet.

goodToKnow.title: Cape Hawke is a climb
goodToKnow.detail: The lookout is a 500 m rainforest climb of about 420 steps to the tower.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Summer, {months}, is the beach season for families, and whales pass offshore from May to November, so the town works across much of the year.
